searchText: It would be nice to have a testnet with regular PoW too, so I guess it is better to have a separate testnet for the merge Post merge there is no need for a public PoW testnet. I do think Ropsten should probably be the *last* testnet to go through The Merge, because it is the one that is *closest* to mainnet (with all of its historic baggage). I assumed that you want to execute the merge on it before the mainnet merge If you plan to make it after - then there is indeed no need for PoW testnet On a related note, I wonder if The Merge is the right time to spin up a mainnet fork testnet? This would be a testnet where we just change network ID (but not chain ID) and lower the difficulty. We would then mirror transactions from mainnet over to the testnet (the subset that remain compatible). This would allow us to test with mainnet state history and close to mainnet transaction volume and shape. That’s a very good idea Or, you can just fork a chain at a certain height and make an ETC-like network We specifically want mainnet transaction volume though, which means shared chain ID so we can mirror transactions over. You can keep the same chain ID Also do note that it is impossible to mirror the entire mainnet without somehow keeping the same tx ordering in the block Yeah, the states would certainly diverge. The goal is to just have them be as *close* as possible to each other. am I understanding correctly that you'll need to have the full mainnet state (in more or less the current form) to run that testnet?, that will be run only in specialized scenarios and only by some handful of devs. Certainly my 2TB NVME will not be able to hold mainnet geth + testnet geth + beaconchain soon enough. Correct, but you could start by copying your state from mainnet. Yeah, you would need a big drive to run this plus mainnet. Isn't it unsafe in some cases to have a testnet with the same Chain ID that is used on the Mainnet? One could ask any user to send it some "test ETH" and the user could do that Though, I see a big value in running such a testnet and we should do this. Just want to be sure that this is gonna be secure for users Users would need to not *do* things on that testnet. The idea is that it wouldn't be *used* directly, it would only receive mirroring. Perhaps some advanced users (core devs) could act on it directly, but that definitely isn't recommended. If users can’t do anything how will the testnet be used for any testing it's used to test mainnet-sized load *not* to give users an enviroment for their own tests (there would be user focused testnets as well) fwiw, Besu created a tool to bloat the state of a testnet when working on 1559. Can also use that if we just want a testnet with X accounts and Y storage lots, where X & Y ~= the mainnet values ... we may even still have a copy of the DB of the 1559 one 🙂 While I think this is situationally useful, the data generated doesn't have the same shape and utilization shape as mainnet data. The closer we can get to real-world usage during test the better. Right, it's not a perfect substitute, but if it's 1/10th the technical complexity and gives us most of the learnings, might be worth doing 🙂 Ah, I think that it is a similar level of complexity and gives us significantly less of the learnings. Though, for some reason that I haven't been able to figure out not everyone agrees with me on the complexity side of things. We briefly discussed it in an ACD and I wasn't able to figure out why some client devs think it would be challenging. I would like to get more information on that if possible.
